faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. For the national minimum wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. This compensates casual employees for not receiving paid leave like annual or sick leave. When using a pay calculator, ensure you add the loading if you are a casual employee. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings, currently at 12% of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your salary. For example, if your annual salary is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is separate from your take-home pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Pay

Converting an hourly wage to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the National Employment Standards. This article uses that assumption unless stated otherwise. The formula is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours per week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. Your fortnightly pay (every two weeks) would be $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280 before tax.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the minimum an award/agreement-free adult employee can be paid. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement, which often sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, listing minimum pay rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check the relevant award for your industry or occupation to ensure you are paid correctly.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual loading is a 25% premium on the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add this loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on a $60,000 salary, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your take-home pay.

### Tax and Medicare

Income tax for 2026–27 uses the resident tax-free threshold: nil tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a single person earning $60,000, tax would be approximately $5,092 plus $1,200 Medicare levy, leaving about $53,708 after tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Stephen Crichton Salary Context

While the **stephen crichton salary** is a topic of interest for rugby league fans, it highlights how annual contracts differ from hourly wages. Top NRL players like Crichton are typically paid an annual salary under a contract, not an hourly rate. Their earnings far exceed the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026, Australian Bureau of Statistics). For most workers, understanding hourly to annual conversion is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. The stephen crichton salary serves as a reminder that high-profile athletes often have complex packages including bonuses and endorsements, unlike standard wage earners.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, as well as estimated tax and super. Remember that the results are estimates based on standard assumptions (38-hour week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no salary sacrifice). Always consult your award or employment contract for exact conditions.

### Fortnightly and Annual Comparisons

Knowing your fortnightly pay helps with budgeting, as many expenses are billed monthly or fortnightly. From the hourly rate, multiply by 76 hours (38 × 2) to get gross fortnightly pay. For example, $26.44 per hour gives $2,009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, the net amount will be lower. Use our [pay guides](/blog) to find award-specific rates and allowances.

### Important Disclaimers

The calculations on this site assume a consistent hourly rate across all weeks, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or the Australian Taxation Office.
